rmt-2016-calc-01.title: Slice by height
rmt-2016-calc-01.body:
The solid is $\{x^2+y^2\le1,\ y^2+z^2\le1,\ x^2+z^2\le1\}$. At height $z$ put $h=\sqrt{1-z^2}$; the cross-section is the square $[-h,h]^2$ intersected with the unit disc. For $|z|\ge\frac1{\sqrt2}$ ($h\le\frac1{\sqrt2}$) the square lies in the disc and has area $4h^2=4(1-z^2)$. For $0\le z<\frac1{\sqrt2}$ the area is $4\left(zh+\frac\pi4-\arcsin z\right)$ (four copies of a disc sector plus two triangles).

With $a=\frac1{\sqrt2}$: $\int_0^a4\left(z\sqrt{1-z^2}+\frac\pi4-\arcsin z\right)dz=\frac{16}3-\frac{7\sqrt2}3$ and $\int_a^14(1-z^2)\,dz=\frac83-\frac{5\sqrt2}3$. The sum is $8-4\sqrt2$ and by symmetry in $z\to-z$ the volume is $2(8-4\sqrt2)=16-8\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $8(2-\sqrt2)$**

rmt-2016-calc-01.title: Polar coordinates
rmt-2016-calc-01.body:
Split into $16$ congruent pieces. In the first octant with $0\le\theta\le\frac\pi4$, the solid lies under $z=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ with $x=r\cos\theta$, so $V=16\int_0^{\pi/4}\int_0^1r\sqrt{1-r^2\cos^2\theta}\,dr\,d\theta=16-8\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $8(2-\sqrt2)$**

rmt-2016-calc-02.title: Asymptotics of Airy's equation
rmt-2016-calc-02.body:
This is Airy's equation. If $\ln y\sim\alpha x^{3/2}$ then $y'\approx\frac32\alpha x^{1/2}y$ and $y''\approx\frac94\alpha^2x\,y$ to leading order. Comparing with $y''=xy$ gives $\frac94\alpha^2=1$, so $\alpha=\pm\frac23$. A generic solution (one with a nonzero $\mathrm{Bi}$ component) grows like $e^{\frac23x^{3/2}}$, so the limit is $\frac23$.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

rmt-2016-calc-03.title: Trigonometric substitution
rmt-2016-calc-03.body:
Put $x=\cos^2\varphi$ and $f(x)=g(\varphi)$. Then $\frac{d}{dx}=-\frac1{\sin2\varphi}\frac d{d\varphi}$, and the equation becomes $g''(\varphi)+g(\varphi)=0$ (the $\cot2\varphi\,g'$ terms cancel). So $g=A\cos\varphi+B\sin\varphi$, i.e. $f=A\sqrt x+B\sqrt{1-x}$. The condition $f'(1)=\frac12$ is finite, which forces $B=0$ (the term $\sqrt{1-x}$ has infinite derivative at $1$), and $f(1)=1$ gives $A=1$: $f(x)=\sqrt x$.

(Check: $f'=\frac12x^{-1/2}$, $f''=-\frac14x^{-3/2}$, and $4x(1-x)f''+2(1-2x)f'+f=x^{-1/2}\left(-(1-x)+(1-2x)+x\right)=0$.)

**Answer: $f(x)=\sqrt x$**

rmt-2016-calc-04.title: Symmetry $x\to\frac\pi2-x$
rmt-2016-calc-04.body:
Substituting $x\mapsto\frac\pi2-x$ turns $\tan x$ into $\cot x$, so $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+\sqrt{\cot x}}=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sqrt{\tan x}\,dx}{1+\sqrt{\tan x}}$. Adding the two expressions: $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}1\,dx=\frac\pi2$, so $I=\frac\pi4$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi4$**

rmt-2016-calc-05.title: Substitute $u=1+\ln x$
rmt-2016-calc-05.body:
Then $x=e^{u-1}$, $dx=e^{u-1}du$, and $u$ runs from $1$ to $2$: $\int_1^2\frac{(u-1)e^{u-1}}{u^2}du=\int_1^2\left(\frac1u-\frac1{u^2}\right)e^{u-1}du$. Note $\frac d{du}\left(\frac{e^{u-1}}u\right)=\frac{e^{u-1}}u-\frac{e^{u-1}}{u^2}$, so the integral is $\left[\frac{e^{u-1}}u\right]_1^2=\frac e2-1$.

**Answer: $\frac e2-1$**

rmt-2016-calc-06.title: Sum of exponentials
rmt-2016-calc-06.body:
With $z=e^{ix}$, $\frac{\sin10x}{\sin x}=\frac{z^{10}-z^{-10}}{z-z^{-1}}=z^9+z^7+\dots+z^{-7}+z^{-9}=\sum_{k\in\{-9,-7,\dots,9\}}e^{ikx}$ (ten terms, all odd frequencies). Squaring gives $\sum_{j,k}e^{i(j+k)x}$; over $[0,\pi]$ every term with $j+k\ne0$ ($j+k$ even and nonzero) integrates to $0$, since $\int_0^\pi\cos(2mx)dx=0$ and the sine parts cancel by symmetry. The terms with $j+k=0$ contribute $1$ each: there are $10$ of them. So the integral is $10\pi$ and the answer is $10$.

**Answer: 10**

rmt-2016-calc-07.title: Gaussian integral
rmt-2016-calc-07.body:
Let $u=\sqrt{-\ln x-1}$, so $x=e^{-u^2-1}$ and $dx=-2ue^{-u^2-1}du$; $x$ from $0$ to $\frac1e$ corresponds to $u$ from $\infty$ to $0$. The integral becomes $\int_0^\infty2e^{-u^2-1}du=\frac1e\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-u^2}du=\frac{\sqrt\pi}e$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt\pi}e$**

rmt-2016-calc-08.title: Law of cosines
rmt-2016-calc-08.body:
Let $x=CX$ and $y=CY$. Equal-area-half means $xy=\frac12\cdot AC\cdot BC=6$. With $\alpha=\angle ACB$, $\cos\alpha=\frac{16+9-4}{2\cdot4\cdot3}=\frac78$, and $XY^2=x^2+y^2-2xy\cos\alpha=x^2+y^2-\frac{21}2$. By AM-GM $x^2+y^2\ge2xy=12$ with equality at $x=y=\sqrt6$, which is allowed ($\sqrt6\le3$ and $\le4$). So $XY^2\ge12-\frac{21}2=\frac32$ and $XY_{\min}=\sqrt{\frac32}=\frac{\sqrt6}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt6}2$**

rmt-2016-calc-10.title: Optimize backwards
rmt-2016-calc-10.body:
Second serve at speed $v$: win probability $p(v)q(v)=\frac{v(150-v)}{15000}$, maximized at $v=75$ with value $\frac{75}{150}\cdot\frac{75}{100}=\frac38$. First serve at speed $v$: $W(v)=p(v)q(v)+(1-p(v))\cdot\frac38=\frac{v(150-v)}{15000}+\frac{3v}{1200}$. $W'(v)=\frac{150-2v}{15000}+\frac{3}{1200}=0$ gives $v=\frac{375}4=93.75\le100$. Then $p=\frac{150-93.75}{150}=\frac38$, $q=\frac{15}{16}$, so $W=\frac38\cdot\frac{15}{16}+\frac58\cdot\frac38=\frac{45}{128}+\frac{30}{128}=\frac{75}{128}$.

**Answer: $\frac{75}{128}$**
